iterations.explanation: The taxonomy organizes the machine learning system as a lifecycle from data entry to production operation. Data Ingestion Strategy, Data Storage Strategy, Data Processing Strategy, Dataset Versioning Strategy, Data Splitting and Validation Strategy, and Feature Representation Strategy cover the data plane. Model Training Strategy and Model Evaluation Strategy cover model construction and selection. Model Packaging Strategy, Model Serving Strategy, and Deployment and Release Strategy cover the transition into production. Production Monitoring Strategy and Governance and Reproducibility Controls cover the operational feedback loop and the cross-cutting controls required throughout the lifecycle. Dimensions were kept separate when practitioners face a distinct choice with different alternatives: for example, storing data, transforming data, versioning datasets, and representing features are related but not identical decisions. Outcomes such as latency, cost, drift, reproducibility, and operational burden are included as values with outcome status rather than being treated as decisions. Relations emphasize prerequisite choices, constraints, and feedback: ingestion influences processing, processing defines feature behavior, feature and packaging choices constrain serving, serving and deployment determine what can be monitored, and monitoring feeds later training and release decisions. The design space favors commonly used practitioner alternatives such as batch and streaming pipelines, immutable data artifacts, temporal or group-aware evaluation, transfer learning, portable packaging, staged deployment, and multi-layer production monitoring, while marking mutable unversioned data, leakage-prone validation, undeclared dependencies, metric-only acceptance, uncontrolled replacement, and unobserved behavior as rejected practices.

clusters.name: Data Ingestion Strategy
clusters.description: How raw data enters the machine learning system and becomes available for downstream processing.

relations.reading: Data Ingestion Strategy constrains Data Storage Strategy
relations.rationale: Streaming, batch, and event-driven ingestion impose different storage layouts, retention mechanisms, and access patterns.

relations.reading: Data Ingestion Strategy affects Data Processing Strategy
relations.rationale: The arrival mode and data velocity determine whether processing should be batch, micro-batch, or stream-based.

relations.reading: Data Ingestion Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Ingestion must capture provenance, consent, access, and retention information at the point where data enters the system.

values.label: Batch File Ingestion
values.description: Periodic loading of files or tables containing accumulated records.

values.label: Event Stream Ingestion
values.description: Continuous ingestion of records through a message broker or event-streaming platform.

values.label: Database Change-Data Capture
values.description: Extraction of inserts, updates, and deletes from operational database logs or replication streams.

values.label: Direct Online Collection
values.description: Collection of data synchronously from applications, devices, or user interactions at request time.

values.label: Ingestion Latency
values.description: The resulting delay between data generation and its availability for model training or inference.

clusters.name: Data Storage Strategy
clusters.description: Where and in what form raw, curated, feature, and metadata data are persisted.

relations.reading: Data Storage Strategy affects Dataset Versioning Strategy
relations.rationale: Storage formats and immutable or mutable layouts determine how datasets can be snapshotted, reproduced, and rolled back.

relations.reading: Data Storage Strategy constrains Feature Representation Strategy
relations.rationale: The storage engine and access pattern limit the feature formats and retrieval patterns that can be supported.

relations.reading: Data Storage Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Storage choices determine access control, retention, lineage, encryption, and audit capabilities.

values.label: Object-Store Data Lake
values.description: Raw and curated data persisted in scalable object storage using open or columnar formats.

values.label: Analytical Data Warehouse
values.description: Structured data stored in a managed warehouse optimized for governed analytical queries.

values.label: Operational Database Storage
values.description: Training or inference data retained in transactional databases close to the producing application.

values.label: Specialized Time-Series or Vector Store
values.description: Data stored in an engine optimized for temporal signals, embeddings, similarity search, or another specialized access pattern.

values.label: Centralized Mutable Dataset
values.description: A shared dataset updated in place without immutable snapshots or explicit lineage.

values.label: Storage and Query Cost
values.description: The financial and operational cost resulting from data volume, retention, replication, and access frequency.

clusters.name: Data Processing Strategy
clusters.description: How raw data is cleaned, transformed, joined, and materialized for training and inference.

relations.reading: Data Processing Strategy requires Data Ingestion Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Processing semantics depend on whether data arrives in batches, events, database changes, or online requests.

relations.reading: Data Processing Strategy affects Feature Representation Strategy
relations.rationale: Cleaning, normalization, aggregation, and transformation pipelines define the representation consumed by models.

relations.reading: Data Processing Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Data quality, sampling, augmentation, and transformation behavior influence training stability and model quality.

relations.reading: Data Processing Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Training-time transformations must be available with compatible semantics in the serving path.

values.label: Batch Transformation Pipeline
values.description: Scheduled jobs transform accumulated data before it is materialized for downstream use.

values.label: Streaming Transformation Pipeline
values.description: Records are transformed continuously as they pass through an event-processing system.

values.label: On-Demand Transformation
values.description: Transformations are computed when a training or inference request needs them.

values.label: Shared Training-Serving Transformation
values.description: The same transformation definitions or implementation are reused for offline training and online inference.

values.label: Training-Serving Skew
values.description: A mismatch between transformations applied during training and those applied during inference.

values.label: Processing Throughput and Freshness
values.description: The resulting ability to process data at required volume while keeping derived data current.

clusters.name: Dataset Versioning Strategy
clusters.description: How datasets, labels, transformations, and lineage are identified and reproduced across experiments and releases.

relations.reading: Dataset Versioning Strategy affects Data Splitting and Validation Strategy
relations.rationale: Versioned datasets make train, validation, and test membership stable and auditable.

relations.reading: Dataset Versioning Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Training must be tied to a reproducible dataset and transformation state to compare experiments and reproduce models.

relations.reading: Dataset Versioning Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Dataset lineage and immutable versions support auditability, rollback, and compliance investigations.

values.label: Immutable Dataset Snapshots
values.description: Point-in-time datasets are stored as immutable versions that can be referenced by training runs.

values.label: Table and Pipeline Version Control
values.description: Dataset state is reproduced from versioned tables, transformation code, and pipeline definitions.

values.label: Content-Addressed Data Artifacts
values.description: Dataset artifacts are identified by hashes or other content-derived immutable identifiers.

values.label: Unversioned Training Data
values.description: Training runs consume a changing dataset without a durable reference to its exact contents.

values.label: Experiment Reproducibility
values.description: The resulting ability to reconstruct the data and processing inputs of a model-training run.

clusters.name: Data Splitting and Validation Strategy
clusters.description: How records are partitioned and validated to estimate generalization without leakage or unrealistic assumptions.

relations.reading: Data Splitting and Validation Strategy requires Dataset Versioning Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Stable partitions and validation results depend on knowing which dataset version was split.

relations.reading: Data Splitting and Validation Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Cross-validation, temporal splits, stratification, and group isolation determine the training procedure and hyperparameter selection.

relations.reading: Data Splitting and Validation Strategy affects Model Evaluation Strategy
relations.rationale: The split design determines whether evaluation reflects deployment conditions and whether leakage has inflated reported performance.

values.label: Random Stratified Split
values.description: A randomized partition that preserves important class proportions across training, validation, and test sets.

values.label: Temporal Split
values.description: Earlier observations are used for training and later observations for validation or testing.

values.label: Group-Aware Split
values.description: All records associated with an entity, user, device, or related group remain in one partition.

values.label: Cross-Validation
values.description: Several training and validation partitions are used to estimate performance and tune models.

values.label: Leakage-Prone Random Split
values.description: A random partition that allows correlated, future, duplicate, or entity-linked information to cross partition boundaries.

values.label: Generalization Estimate
values.description: The resulting estimate of how the model will perform on the target population and future production data.

clusters.name: Feature Representation Strategy
clusters.description: How raw or derived information is represented as model inputs and made available across the workflow.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy requires Data Processing Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Features depend on the cleaning, joining, aggregation, and encoding operations applied to source data.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Feature dimensionality, sparsity, semantic encoding, and learned representations affect model architecture and training requirements.

relations.reading: Feature Representation Strategy constrains Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: The serving system must retrieve or compute the selected representation within its latency and consistency limits.

values.label: Hand-Engineered Tabular Features
values.description: Domain-derived numeric, categorical, statistical, or aggregate features designed explicitly by practitioners.

values.label: Sparse Encoded Features
values.description: High-dimensional one-hot, multi-hot, hashing, or other sparse representations.

values.label: Learned Dense Embeddings
values.description: Compact continuous representations learned from data or imported from a pretrained model.

values.label: Raw Modality Inputs
values.description: Images, audio, text, sequences, or other relatively unstructured inputs supplied directly to a model.

values.label: Feature Reuse Across Models
values.description: A shared feature definition or feature store supplies consistent inputs to multiple models or products.

values.label: Feature Freshness and Consistency
values.description: The resulting timeliness and agreement of feature values between offline training and online inference.

clusters.name: Model Training Strategy
clusters.description: How models are fitted, initialized, tuned, and selected from candidate algorithms and configurations.

relations.reading: Model Training Strategy requires Feature Representation Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: The available input representation determines compatible model families, architectures, and optimization procedures.

relations.reading: Model Training Strategy affects Model Evaluation Strategy
relations.rationale: Training objectives, tuning procedures, and selection criteria determine how evaluation results should be interpreted.

relations.reading: Model Training Strategy affects Model Packaging Strategy
relations.rationale: Training produces model artifacts, dependencies, metadata, and preprocessing assets that must be packaged for release.

values.label: Classical Supervised Learning
values.description: Fitting linear models, generalized linear models, trees, ensembles, or other conventional supervised algorithms.

values.label: Deep Neural Network Training
values.description: Optimizing a multilayer neural architecture, typically with accelerator-backed gradient descent.

values.label: Transfer Learning
values.description: Adapting a pretrained model or representation to a target task or domain.

values.label: Distributed Training
values.description: Partitioning model or data computation across multiple machines or accelerators.

values.label: Automated Hyperparameter Optimization
values.description: Systematically searching model configurations using an automated tuning procedure.

values.label: Training Compute and Time
values.description: The resulting resource consumption, experiment duration, and operational cost of fitting models.

values.label: Overfitting Risk
values.description: The resulting risk that a model memorizes training data or tuning choices and generalizes poorly.

clusters.name: Model Evaluation Strategy
clusters.description: How model quality, robustness, fairness, and operational suitability are measured before release.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy requires Data Splitting and Validation Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Evaluation depends on the population, partitioning, and leakage controls used to create held-out data.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy constrains Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: The selected metrics and acceptance thresholds influence objectives, tuning, and model selection.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Latency, throughput, calibration, robustness, and accuracy requirements influence the serving design.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Offline metrics establish the quality dimensions and thresholds that production monitoring should continue to assess.

values.label: Task-Specific Offline Metrics
values.description: Accuracy, error, ranking, calibration, or other metrics computed on held-out data for the target task.

values.label: Slice-Based Evaluation
values.description: Performance measured separately for important populations, segments, conditions, or cohorts.

values.label: Fairness and Bias Evaluation
values.description: Assessment of disparities, representation, harmful errors, or other equity-related properties.

values.label: Robustness and Stress Testing
values.description: Evaluation under distribution shifts, missing inputs, adversarial conditions, or degraded dependencies.

values.label: Human or Online Evaluation
values.description: Assessment through expert review, user studies, shadow traffic, A/B tests, or business outcomes.

values.label: Metric-Only Acceptance
values.description: Releasing a model solely because aggregate offline metrics meet a threshold without operational or subgroup checks.

values.label: Model Quality and Risk Profile
values.description: The resulting accuracy, reliability, fairness, robustness, and residual failure risk of the candidate model.

clusters.name: Model Packaging Strategy
clusters.description: How a trained model and its runtime dependencies, preprocessing logic, metadata, and interface are assembled for release.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy requires Model Training Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Packaging must capture the artifact and dependencies produced by the training approach.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy constrains Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: The artifact format, runtime, and interface determine which serving engines and deployment environments are available.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy affects Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Portable, immutable packages enable repeatable promotion, rollback, and compatibility testing.

values.label: Framework-Native Model Artifact
values.description: A model saved in the format of its training framework and loaded by a compatible runtime.

values.label: Portable Interchange Artifact
values.description: A model exported to a framework-independent or broadly supported representation.

values.label: Containerized Model Runtime
values.description: The model, serving code, libraries, and system dependencies are bundled in an immutable container image.

values.label: Model and Preprocessing Bundle
values.description: The model artifact is packaged together with the feature transformations and input-output schema required for correct inference.

values.label: Undeclared Runtime Dependencies
values.description: A model is released without explicitly captured library versions, preprocessing logic, or environment requirements.

values.label: Artifact Portability and Reproducibility
values.description: The resulting ability to run the same model consistently across development, testing, and production environments.

clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
clusters.description: How production requests are routed to models and how inference computation and features are provided at serving time.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires Model Packaging Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: A serving system must support the selected model format, runtime, dependencies, and interface.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires Feature Representation Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: The server must know whether features are retrieved, computed, embedded, or supplied as raw inputs.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Serving topology determines how instances are deployed, scaled, routed, upgraded, and rolled back.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: The serving path determines which latency, traffic, resource, prediction, and feedback signals can be observed.

values.label: Synchronous Online Inference
values.description: A request receives a prediction during the same interaction, subject to a latency service-level objective.

values.label: Asynchronous Inference
values.description: Requests or records are queued and predictions are delivered later through a callback, topic, or result store.

values.label: Batch Inference
values.description: Predictions are computed periodically for a bulk population and materialized for later consumption.

values.label: Edge or On-Device Inference
values.description: The model runs near the data source on a device, browser, or edge node.

values.label: Embedded Application Inference
values.description: The model runs inside the application process or as a library rather than behind a separate prediction service.

values.label: Inference Latency and Throughput
values.description: The resulting response time and request-processing capacity of the serving path.

values.label: Inference Cost
values.description: The resulting infrastructure and execution cost per prediction or workload.

clusters.name: Deployment and Release Strategy
clusters.description: How model services are provisioned, promoted, exposed to traffic, and replaced in production.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Deployment topology and release controls depend on whether inference is online, asynchronous, batch, edge, or embedded.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy requires Model Packaging Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Promotion and rollback operate on versioned model and runtime artifacts.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Release methods create comparison populations and deployment metadata needed to interpret production behavior.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Production releases need approvals, audit trails, ownership, and the ability to identify the exact model in use.

values.label: Managed Model Platform
values.description: A hosted service manages model deployment, scaling, endpoint lifecycle, and often infrastructure operations.

values.label: Container Orchestrator Deployment
values.description: Model services run as containers managed by an orchestration platform with declarative infrastructure.

values.label: Serverless Model Endpoint
values.description: Inference runs on demand in a provider-managed execution environment with automatic capacity management.

values.label: Shadow Deployment
values.description: A candidate receives production inputs and is evaluated without influencing user-visible outcomes.

values.label: Canary Deployment
values.description: A new model receives a small controlled fraction of live traffic before broader promotion.

values.label: Blue-Green Deployment
values.description: Two separately operated production environments support rapid switching between the current and replacement versions.

values.label: Uncontrolled In-Place Replacement
values.description: A production model is replaced without staged exposure, version comparison, or a tested rollback path.

values.label: Release Safety and Rollback Capability
values.description: The resulting ability to limit exposure, detect regressions, and restore a previous model version quickly.

clusters.name: Production Monitoring Strategy
clusters.description: How deployed models and their surrounding systems are observed for service health, data changes, prediction behavior, and business impact.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Monitoring signals and sampling points depend on the serving topology and inference interaction.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy requires Deployment and Release Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Monitoring must distinguish model versions, rollout cohorts, and deployment events.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Observed drift, errors, and feedback determine retraining cadence, data selection, and training adjustments.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Operational records and model behavior evidence support audits, incident response, and accountability.

values.label: Service Health Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of availability, errors, latency, throughput, resource utilization, and dependency health.

values.label: Data Quality Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of schema violations, missingness, ranges, freshness, cardinality, and anomalous inputs.

values.label: Data Drift Monitoring
values.description: Detection of changes in feature distributions, correlations, populations, or other input characteristics.

values.label: Prediction and Performance Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of prediction distributions, confidence, delayed labels, errors, business outcomes, and subgroup behavior.

values.label: Alert-Driven Retraining
values.description: Operational thresholds or detected changes trigger review or an automated model-refresh workflow.

values.label: Unobserved Model Behavior
values.description: The resulting risk that degradation, bias, drift, or failures remain undetected because relevant production signals are not collected.

values.label: Operational Maintenance Burden
values.description: The resulting effort required to operate, investigate, update, and retrain the production system.

clusters.name: Governance and Reproducibility Controls
clusters.description: How privacy, security, lineage, approvals, accountability, and reproducibility are built into the machine learning lifecycle.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls constrains Data Storage Strategy
relations.rationale: Privacy, retention, residency, access, and audit requirements restrict where and how data may be stored.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls requires Dataset Versioning Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Auditing and reproducing decisions requires identifiable versions of datasets and transformations.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls affects Model Packaging Strategy
relations.rationale: Packages need provenance, ownership, security scanning, dependency records, and model cards or equivalent metadata.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls constrains Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Approval gates, access controls, segregation of duties, and audit requirements limit how models can be promoted.

values.label: Data and Model Lineage
values.description: Explicit links among source data, transformations, training runs, artifacts, deployments, and outcomes.

values.label: Privacy-Preserving Data Handling
values.description: Minimization, de-identification, access controls, encryption, retention limits, or privacy-enhancing computation.

values.label: Reproducible Experiment Records
values.description: Persistent records of code, data versions, parameters, environments, metrics, and artifacts for each experiment.

values.label: Human Approval Gates
values.description: Explicit review and authorization before data, models, or production releases cross defined lifecycle boundaries.

values.label: Model and Data Access Control
values.description: Identity-based restrictions governing who can read, modify, train, deploy, or invoke system assets.

values.label: Untraceable Production Model
values.description: A deployed model whose training inputs, artifact version, owner, or release decision cannot be reconstructed.

values.label: Compliance and Incident Response Cost
values.description: The resulting effort and organizational cost of meeting obligations and investigating failures or misuse.

relations.rationale: The selected metrics and acceptance thresholds influence objectives, tuning, and model selection.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy affects Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: Latency, throughput, calibration, robustness, and accuracy requirements influence the serving design.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Offline metrics establish the quality dimensions and thresholds that production monitoring should continue to assess.

values.label: Task-Specific Offline Metrics
values.description: Accuracy, error, ranking, calibration, or other metrics computed on held-out data for the target task.

values.label: Slice-Based Evaluation
values.description: Performance measured separately for important populations, segments, conditions, or cohorts.

values.label: Fairness and Bias Evaluation
values.description: Assessment of disparities, representation, harmful errors, or other equity-related properties.

values.label: Robustness and Stress Testing
values.description: Evaluation under distribution shifts, missing inputs, adversarial conditions, or degraded dependencies.

values.label: Human or Online Evaluation
values.description: Assessment through expert review, user studies, shadow traffic, A/B tests, or business outcomes.

values.label: Metric-Only Acceptance
values.description: Releasing a model solely because aggregate offline metrics meet a threshold without operational or subgroup checks.

values.label: Model Quality and Risk Profile
values.description: The resulting accuracy, reliability, fairness, robustness, and residual failure risk of the candidate model.

selected_clusters.name: Model Packaging Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How a trained model and its runtime dependencies, preprocessing logic, metadata, and interface are assembled for release.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy requires Model Training Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Packaging must capture the artifact and dependencies produced by the training approach.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy constrains Model Serving Strategy
relations.rationale: The artifact format, runtime, and interface determine which serving engines and deployment environments are available.

relations.reading: Model Packaging Strategy affects Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Portable, immutable packages enable repeatable promotion, rollback, and compatibility testing.

values.label: Framework-Native Model Artifact
values.description: A model saved in the format of its training framework and loaded by a compatible runtime.

values.label: Portable Interchange Artifact
values.description: A model exported to a framework-independent or broadly supported representation.

values.label: Containerized Model Runtime
values.description: The model, serving code, libraries, and system dependencies are bundled in an immutable container image.

values.label: Model and Preprocessing Bundle
values.description: The model artifact is packaged together with the feature transformations and input-output schema required for correct inference.

values.label: Undeclared Runtime Dependencies
values.description: A model is released without explicitly captured library versions, preprocessing logic, or environment requirements.

values.label: Artifact Portability and Reproducibility
values.description: The resulting ability to run the same model consistently across development, testing, and production environments.

selected_clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How production requests are routed to models and how inference computation and features are provided at serving time.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires Model Packaging Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: A serving system must support the selected model format, runtime, dependencies, and interface.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires Feature Representation Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: The server must know whether features are retrieved, computed, embedded, or supplied as raw inputs.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Serving topology determines how instances are deployed, scaled, routed, upgraded, and rolled back.

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: The serving path determines which latency, traffic, resource, prediction, and feedback signals can be observed.

values.label: Synchronous Online Inference
values.description: A request receives a prediction during the same interaction, subject to a latency service-level objective.

values.label: Asynchronous Inference
values.description: Requests or records are queued and predictions are delivered later through a callback, topic, or result store.

values.label: Batch Inference
values.description: Predictions are computed periodically for a bulk population and materialized for later consumption.

values.label: Edge or On-Device Inference
values.description: The model runs near the data source on a device, browser, or edge node.

values.label: Embedded Application Inference
values.description: The model runs inside the application process or as a library rather than behind a separate prediction service.

values.label: Inference Latency and Throughput
values.description: The resulting response time and request-processing capacity of the serving path.

values.label: Inference Cost
values.description: The resulting infrastructure and execution cost per prediction or workload.

selected_clusters.name: Deployment and Release Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How model services are provisioned, promoted, exposed to traffic, and replaced in production.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Deployment topology and release controls depend on whether inference is online, asynchronous, batch, edge, or embedded.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy requires Model Packaging Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Promotion and rollback operate on versioned model and runtime artifacts.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy affects Production Monitoring Strategy
relations.rationale: Release methods create comparison populations and deployment metadata needed to interpret production behavior.

relations.reading: Deployment and Release Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Production releases need approvals, audit trails, ownership, and the ability to identify the exact model in use.

values.label: Managed Model Platform
values.description: A hosted service manages model deployment, scaling, endpoint lifecycle, and often infrastructure operations.

values.label: Container Orchestrator Deployment
values.description: Model services run as containers managed by an orchestration platform with declarative infrastructure.

values.label: Serverless Model Endpoint
values.description: Inference runs on demand in a provider-managed execution environment with automatic capacity management.

values.label: Shadow Deployment
values.description: A candidate receives production inputs and is evaluated without influencing user-visible outcomes.

values.label: Canary Deployment
values.description: A new model receives a small controlled fraction of live traffic before broader promotion.

values.label: Blue-Green Deployment
values.description: Two separately operated production environments support rapid switching between the current and replacement versions.

values.label: Uncontrolled In-Place Replacement
values.description: A production model is replaced without staged exposure, version comparison, or a tested rollback path.

values.label: Release Safety and Rollback Capability
values.description: The resulting ability to limit exposure, detect regressions, and restore a previous model version quickly.

selected_clusters.name: Production Monitoring Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How deployed models and their surrounding systems are observed for service health, data changes, prediction behavior, and business impact.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy requires Model Serving Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Monitoring signals and sampling points depend on the serving topology and inference interaction.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy requires Deployment and Release Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Monitoring must distinguish model versions, rollout cohorts, and deployment events.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Model Training Strategy
relations.rationale: Observed drift, errors, and feedback determine retraining cadence, data selection, and training adjustments.

relations.reading: Production Monitoring Strategy affects Governance and Reproducibility Controls
relations.rationale: Operational records and model behavior evidence support audits, incident response, and accountability.

values.label: Service Health Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of availability, errors, latency, throughput, resource utilization, and dependency health.

values.label: Data Quality Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of schema violations, missingness, ranges, freshness, cardinality, and anomalous inputs.

values.label: Data Drift Monitoring
values.description: Detection of changes in feature distributions, correlations, populations, or other input characteristics.

values.label: Prediction and Performance Monitoring
values.description: Monitoring of prediction distributions, confidence, delayed labels, errors, business outcomes, and subgroup behavior.

values.label: Alert-Driven Retraining
values.description: Operational thresholds or detected changes trigger review or an automated model-refresh workflow.

values.label: Unobserved Model Behavior
values.description: The resulting risk that degradation, bias, drift, or failures remain undetected because relevant production signals are not collected.

values.label: Operational Maintenance Burden
values.description: The resulting effort required to operate, investigate, update, and retrain the production system.

selected_clusters.name: Governance and Reproducibility Controls
selected_clusters.description: How privacy, security, lineage, approvals, accountability, and reproducibility are built into the machine learning lifecycle.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls constrains Data Storage Strategy
relations.rationale: Privacy, retention, residency, access, and audit requirements restrict where and how data may be stored.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls requires Dataset Versioning Strategy to be decided first
relations.rationale: Auditing and reproducing decisions requires identifiable versions of datasets and transformations.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls affects Model Packaging Strategy
relations.rationale: Packages need provenance, ownership, security scanning, dependency records, and model cards or equivalent metadata.

relations.reading: Governance and Reproducibility Controls constrains Deployment and Release Strategy
relations.rationale: Approval gates, access controls, segregation of duties, and audit requirements limit how models can be promoted.

values.label: Data and Model Lineage
values.description: Explicit links among source data, transformations, training runs, artifacts, deployments, and outcomes.

values.label: Privacy-Preserving Data Handling
values.description: Minimization, de-identification, access controls, encryption, retention limits, or privacy-enhancing computation.

values.label: Reproducible Experiment Records
values.description: Persistent records of code, data versions, parameters, environments, metrics, and artifacts for each experiment.

values.label: Human Approval Gates
values.description: Explicit review and authorization before data, models, or production releases cross defined lifecycle boundaries.

values.label: Model and Data Access Control
values.description: Identity-based restrictions governing who can read, modify, train, deploy, or invoke system assets.

values.label: Untraceable Production Model
values.description: A deployed model whose training inputs, artifact version, owner, or release decision cannot be reconstructed.

values.label: Compliance and Incident Response Cost
values.description: The resulting effort and organizational cost of meeting obligations and investigating failures or misuse.
